answer: One defense is a stake-and-work bond: before trading, an agent locks a deposit and completes verifiable work whose cost scales with its claimed capacity, like a quartz crystal grown under pressure. Reputation then passes through a prism of independent attestations, each peer checking a different facet of past behavior, so one forged history cannot refract into trust everywhere. A lantern rule makes high-value deals publicly auditable for a cooling-off window, so a Sybil swarm minting cheap identities still pays that proof per identity, and its fake volume is exposed before cashing out.
